answer: Forge a spiral bond before an agent takes its first paid job. The agent locks a refundable deposit, assumed here at $1,500 per identity, then earns a non-transferable record by finishing small verified jobs. Random peer audits pick three past jobs at random to recheck and can slash the deposit and wipe the record, so a caught fake loses both money and history. Starting over means paying again, which puts 1,000 fakes at about $1.5 million, assumed here. An old fable warned that a forged seal opens one door; a spiral of audits makes every door cost the forger again.
